tools.name: beamline_find
tools.description:
Call this whenever the person asks for any screen, page or control (a booking screen, a data table, a date range picker): returns the best Beamline screens and parts for it, with their kind of app, free or paid, page, picture and what each screen is built from. Free to call; no sign-in.
Pass their w

tools.name: beamline_capabilities
tools.description:
The complete Beamline library and how to choose from it: a selection guide (screens and kits, data → control, screen craft, looks and install), then every screen and component with what it is for and what to use instead.
To find parts for a request, call beamline_find first. Call this before designi

tools.name: beamline_component
tools.description:
Exact details of Beamline elements: the import, required and typed props, states, keyboard, motion, the parts to style and working examples to copy.
Call it for every element you chose, blocks included, before writing code with it; never guess props. Many ids come back in parts: call again with the

tools.name: beamline_install
tools.description:
One command that adds the chosen Beamline elements and a look (default prism) to the app: only those packages, one stylesheet and the look.
Pass every element the screens need in one call; call it again to add more later. Run the command in the app folder, import the stylesheet once and pass the ins

tools.name: beamline_picture
tools.description: Inspect a candidate's layout and states, compare plausible choices, or show the person how a part looks. Returns one labelled states sheet in dark or light Prism and a public URL. Pictures of 🔒 elements are available too; their code still needs access. Choose pictures that resolve a design question

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "beamline_capabilities" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
